projects.title: Thesis, Nonlinear Seismic Analysis: Three Resilience Techniques
projects.meta: 2024 · Academic Research · La Union, Philippines
projects.summary: A five-story school study comparing seismic-response strategies through time-history analysis.
projects.body: Context Problem: Existing 5-story public school structure in Agoo, La Union lacked adequate seismic resilience documentation for Seismic Zone IV conditions. Client/Use: Academic thesis research, Technological Institute of the Philippines. Role Responsibilities: Designed and analyzed three independent seismic resilience systems, base isolation, buckling-restrained braces (BRBs), and steel-plate shear walls, and compared their performance using nonlinear time history analysis. Tools: ETABS, SAP2000, NSCP 2015, ASCE 7. Process Modeled the existing structure and applied each retrofit system independently. Ran nonlinear time history analysis using ground motion records scaled to site hazard levels. Evaluated inter-story drift, base shear, and floor acceleration responses across all three systems. Key Challenge: Calibrating nonlinear material properties for each system, required iterative pushover runs before committing to time history analysis. Results All three systems demonstrated measurable improvement over the unretrofitted baseline. Comparative findings documented per NSCP 2015 performance objectives.
contributions: Time history and nonlinear pushover analyses for strength, stiffness, and resilience
Comparative evaluation of seismic techniques with design recommendations

projects.title: CV Data Extractor — Borderless PDF to Excel
projects.meta: 2025–2026 · Personal Automation Tool · Check Voucher Processing
projects.summary: Python extraction of borderless voucher reports using layout positions and persistent date context.
projects.body: Context Problem: Check Voucher (CV) summary reports come out of the source system as text-based PDFs with no visible table gridlines, so standard table-extraction approaches fail. Manually retyping CV numbers, payees, and amounts into Excel was slow and error-prone. Client/Use: Internal tool for converting CV summary PDFs into itemized Excel data for reconciliation and record-keeping. Role Responsibilities: Sole developer. Designed the position-based parsing logic since there were no borders to key off of. Tools: Python, pdfplumber, pandas. Process Words are grouped into lines by vertical position rather than relying on table borders. Header rows are detected by keyword ("CV NUMBER", "AMOUNT", "CHECK"), and their word x-positions become column boundaries that every subsequent data row is bucketed against. Key Challenge: "DATE TRANS" headers are frequently separated from their table by a page break, so the script carries the current date forward continuously across pages until a new date header appears. Subtotal rows, blank rows, and wrapped headers are auto-skipped via pattern matching on the CV number format. Results Reliable extraction of Date Trans, CV Number, Payee, Gross Amount, and Net Amount from borderless PDFs directly into a clean Excel file, with zero manual retyping.
contributions: Position-based column detection with no reliance on visible table borders or gridlines
Date-carry-forward logic that survives page breaks separating headers from their data
Regex-driven row validation to auto-skip subtotals, blanks, and wrapped header rows

projects.title: Expense Monitoring Normalizer
projects.meta: 2025–2026 · Personal Automation Tool · Cost Control Data Flattening
projects.summary: Python cleanup of inconsistent Excel expense sheets into a consistent reporting structure.
projects.body: Context Problem: The expense monitoring workbook is formatted for human presentation, one sheet per supplier, merged/grouped fields, subtotal and month-label rows scattered throughout, which makes it unusable for pivoting, dashboards, or any real analysis. Client/Use: Internal cost control tool to convert a presentation-formatted workbook into an analysis-ready dataset. Role Responsibilities: Sole developer. Reverse-engineered the fixed column layout directly from the live workbook and encoded it as a repeatable transform. Tools: Python, openpyxl, pandas. Process Each supplier sheet is located dynamically by its header row ("NO. OF DELIVER..."), and a fixed column-offset map is applied from that header row onward. Grouped fields (RR No., RR Date, PO No., Supplier Name) are blank on continuation rows in the source, so the script forward-fills them from the last group-start row. Subtotal rows, grand-total rows, month-label rows, and blank rows are all identified and stripped. The "Balance to Pay" total, which lives on its own row per sheet, is captured and broadcast onto every item row from that sheet so it survives the flattening. Output dates are coerced to real datetime values and the Excel output is written with proper number formatting and column widths. Results Every supplier sheet, however inconsistently it was formatted, is flattened into one normalized transactional table, ready for pivot tables, dashboards, or further automation.
contributions: Dynamic header detection per sheet, no hardcoded row numbers, survives layout drift across supplier tabs
Group-aware forward-fill logic for merged/grouped fields (RR No., PO No., Supplier Name)
Automatic stripping of subtotal, grand-total, month-label, and blank rows with balance broadcasting

sections.title: Project overview
sections.text: Pandarithm combines my background in civil engineering with my interest in programming, numerical methods and engineering automation. Its modules cover beam analysis, truss analysis, reinforced concrete design, steel design and related workflows, with individual features at different stages of development and validation.

sections.title: My contribution
sections.text: Project Creator, Engineering Logic Developer & Validation Lead. Developed engineering approaches, mathematical formulations, pseudocode and algorithm flowcharts, with AI-assisted coding supporting implementation, debugging and refinement. My role extends beyond defining software requirements: I translate engineering theory into computational procedures and check whether implemented calculations behave as intended.

sections.title: Engineering methodology
items: Understand the engineering problem: identify governing equations, assumptions, boundary conditions, inputs and expected outputs.
Develop the calculation approach: derive or adapt mathematical expressions and establish pseudocode and the calculation sequence.
Implement the logic: translate the approach into software, using AI-assisted coding where useful.
Verify manually: solve representative problems independently and compare the results with the software.
Benchmark the results: compare against established reference solutions and investigate discrepancies.
Refine and retest: correct calculation, numerical precision and decimal-related errors identified during verification.

sections.title: Example: distributed-load analysis
sections.text: One area of development involved extending beam calculations to handle different distributed-load configurations. I worked from the underlying structural equations to formulate a generalized calculation approach, rather than relying entirely on separate hardcoded expressions for each configuration. The objective was to support more flexible load representations while preserving consistent structural-analysis behavior.

sections.title: Verification and quality control
sections.text: Engineering software must be evaluated on the correctness of its calculations, not simply whether it produces a result. I use independent manual solutions and benchmark comparisons to evaluate computational outputs. Where discrepancies appear, I investigate the calculations, including decimal precision, numerical implementation and the assumptions used in the comparison. This verification process remains ongoing.

sections.title: Current status and future direction
sections.text: Pandarithm remains an actively developed public beta. My next priorities include expanding systematic test coverage, improving calculation traceability, refining engineering reports and validating individual modules before treating them as dependable design tools. The long-term objective is an engineering platform combining reliable calculations, understandable procedures and practical workflows for civil and structural engineering.
